svg.text: Printune: how the app flows
Kalico plugin + Mainsail page. Every test is a print (or a measurement) followed by a pick; results go into Orca presets, machine values into printer.cfg. State: branch initial-import, 2026-10-15.
PRINTUNE macro (Mainsail console)
The only visible macro. Opens a button menu with every workflow below; each step
then talks to you through Mainsail prompts.
Greyed buttons when a tool is missing (no accelerometer, not CoreXY, no
Shake&Tune); tapping one links to the tool's docs.
Printune page (Mainsail sidebar)
Same workflows with more options: setup form, live progress, big pick buttons,
babystep buttons, graphs, preset download. Made for phones down to 320 px wide.
Picks can be made on the page or with the console prompts.
0. Pre-flight
Once per printer, before any filament
1. Standard profile tuning
Tuning Wizard (big blue button), per filament
2. Advanced tuning
Per filament, after the wizard; same preset
3. Expert mode
Your own workflows (planned)
Machine setup (required before any test print)
Bed area: defaults to the bed mesh area (mesh_min /
mesh_max) cut to the axis limits; typed in when there is no
bed mesh.
Measured by you: toolhead box (−X, +X, −Y, +Y from the
nozzle), bed to X beam height at Z=0, and nozzle protrusion
below the rest of the toolhead.
Risk notice: Printune and its authors take zero
responsibility; you confirm you measured the values.
Changing any value clears the acceptance.
Until done, every printing test is locked (wizard, single
tests, Advanced, Orca and command line). Session files
carry the geometry and are refused if it no longer matches.
printer.cfg [printune]: bed_area, toolhead_box, gantry_height,
nozzle_protrusion, setup_accepted
Belt tension (accelerometer pluck)
Needs CoreXY + an accelerometer on the toolhead
([resonance_tester]); otherwise greyed out.
Set the target frequency from your build guide (±1 / ±5 Hz)
and 3 or 5 plucks. The toolhead parks in the middle so the
belt span is known.
Hands off for 1.5 s: fans and motors are recorded and
subtracted later.
Pluck belt A like a guitar string, about once a second.
Printune finds each pluck, takes its frequency (checks for
a tone at half the strongest peak) and shows the average
against the target.
Then belt B. CoreXY belts pull on each other, so both are
measured every round.
Shows: A 104 Hz (avg of 5), 6 Hz low · nothing stored; raw
recordings saved in printune_exports/recordings for download
Turn advice, repeat
First rough: both belts to about 90-100 Hz.
Then small turns: 'Tighten belt B about 3/8 turn, then
measure both again'. It learns Hz per turn and how much one
belt drags the other from each turn you report.
Done when both are within belt_tolerance (2 Hz) of the
target and of each other.
Advice only
Loop: measure A, measure B, turn, until both are in tolerance.
Shake&Tune belt graph (optional)
Offered when the belts are done, if Shake&Tune is
installed: runs its belt comparison and shows the graph
under the prompt and on the page.
Not installed: greyed button linking to the Shake&Tune
project.
Graph only
Z offset (starting value)
The printer's own paper test: PROBE_CALIBRATE with a probe,
BEACON_CALIBRATE with a Beacon, Z_ENDSTOP_CALIBRATE without
a probe.
Printune homes, levels the gantry (Z tilt / QGL) if it can
and moves to the middle of the bed. Lower the nozzle until
the paper drags, Accept, Save config.
Redo after a nozzle or build plate swap. The first layer
test fine-tunes it while printing.
printer.cfg: probe z_offset / position_endstop (SAVE_CONFIG)
Hands-on tools (no print, any time)
Extruder calibration
Mark the filament 120 mm above the extruder, extrude 100
mm, type what is left. Printune computes the new
rotation_distance.
printer.cfg: rotation_distance (stays fixed; per-filament differences
go in Flow)
Extrude-in-air flow check
Extrudes 100 mm at a chosen mm³/s; raise it until less than
100 mm goes in. A quick check next to the printed max flow
tower.
Advice: a value for Max volumetric speed
Recordings and reset
PRINTUNE_RECORD SECONDS=10 NAME=… saves any accelerometer
recording where Mainsail can download it.
'Reset after cancel' clears a stuck session.
Files in printune_exports/
Setup
Pick the filament type (PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA, PC, PA, TPU…),
then the nozzle range from the box and the bed temperature.
Defaults come from the type.
Preset name: '<type> Printune' (rename on the page). Heat
soak on/off is only asked when the printer is marked
enclosed.
Run the whole wizard, or a single test from the same list.
Heat soak (enclosed printers only)
Extruder heater off, toolhead parked as far from the bed as
possible; the nozzle thermistor reads the chamber. Ends
when that reading levels off (between soak_min and
soak_max), or Skip.
The printer stays hot between all tests that follow.
First layer squish
Prints 9 patches of 25×25 mm over the whole bed. Babystep
with ±0.01 / ±0.05 mm while they print.
'Squish is good', or 'Print 4 more patches' to check the
new offset.
Fine-tunes the pre-flight Z offset (machine setting):
Z_OFFSET_APPLY_PROBE + SAVE_CONFIG; never in a filament preset
Pressure advance
A row of hollow frames, one per value (0-0.08 in 0.005
steps). Each edge prints slow-fast-slow, so a wrong value
shows a bulge or gap where the speed changes.
Pick the most even frame; optional fine pass in 0.001
steps.
Filament › Pressure advance (Enable ticked)
Flow (extrusion multiplier)
30×30×3 mm cubes at −4 … +4 % flow, numbered, printed with
the picked PA.
Pick the smoothest top surface; optional fine pass in 0.5 %
steps.
Filament › Flow ratio
Retraction and temperature
Up to 4 towers across the temperature range, hottest first,
each with rings at 0-1.0 mm retraction.
Pick the cleanest tower (temperature), then the ring 1-2
above where stringing stops. Skippable: direct drive often
needs no tuning.
Filament › Nozzle temperature + retraction (SET_RETRACTION in
filament start G-code, or retraction overrides)
On small beds the tests spread over several plates; Printune pauses
with 'clear the plate'.
Results and preset
Summary of every pick. Download the Orca filament preset
(JSON) from the page and import it.
Values are applied live only during the session; the
printer's own values come back afterwards.
printune_exports/<name>.json → Orca filament preset (single
source of truth)
Input shaper (last)
Needs an accelerometer and [input_shaper]; otherwise greyed
(link: Kalico 'Measuring Resonances').
Runs Kalico's SHAPER_CALIBRATE: shows the pick per axis and
the highest acceleration that keeps corners sharp. On right
away; 'Save to printer.cfg' runs SAVE_CONFIG.
With Shake&Tune: its axis graphs run from the same step.
If the shaper changed: offers a pressure advance re-check.
printer.cfg: shaper_type / shaper_freq per axis
Setup (same as the wizard)
Use the wizard's preset name: Advanced prints with the
wizard's temperature, PA, flow and retraction, and adds its
results to that preset (fields it did not test are kept). A
different filament type gets a new preset instead.
Heat soak again if enclosed. Each step is skippable and can
also run alone.
2a
Cooling: fan %
Overhang blocks, one per fan speed (PLA/PETG 40/70/100 %,
ABS/ASA 20-80 %, PC/PA from 0 %), with 30° to 70° overhang
bands. The outer wall prints at its normal speed; layers
are padded to a typical layer time.
Pick the lowest fan % whose overhangs look good. One
constant fan (varying fan causes banding).
Filament › Cooling: fan min = fan max, overhang fan, keep fan
always on
2b
Cooling: minimum layer time
A cone printed on its own at that fan %, constant speed, no
slowdown: layer time falls with height (ABS 26 s, PLA 16 s
down to 1 s), marker every 2 s.
Pick the marker where the tip starts to melt, sag or curl.
Printune adds 3 s; for ABS it flags results far from about
15 s. Curling at low fan can also be bed adhesion.
Filament › Cooling: slow down layer time (Orca's minimum layer
time)
Runs after the soak, so it matches your chamber temperature and part
cooling.
Bridges
Strips bridging 20, 40 and 60 mm between 4 mm pillars, in
three passes, each building on the pick before it.
Fan: from the cooling pick up to 100 % (skipped if that is
already 100 %). Speed: 0.6 to 2 × the bridge speed. Flow:
Pick the cleanest, flattest strip in each pass.
Filament › Overhang/bridge fan speed
Process › Bridge speed, bridge flow ratio (a small process
preset to import)
Max volumetric flow tower
A 60 mm round single-wall spiral. Flow rises in 3 mm bands
(default 5-30 mm³/s, TPU 1-12); a small bump marks every 5
mm³/s. Line 1.5 × nozzle wide, 0.75 × nozzle tall.
Nothing slows it: corners, speed limits and acceleration
are checked; bands the printer can't reach are dropped with
a warning.
Pick the band (or type a height) where the wall gets rough
or weak. Printune proposes 90 % of it and shows the
matching mm/s at 0.2 × 0.45 mm.
Filament › Max volumetric speed
Method as Orca's own: flow = start + height × step, minus a 10-20 %
margin. Printed last, alone on its own plate: at 79 mm it is far
taller than the gantry clearance.
Max speed and acceleration (machine)
PLANNED
Fast test moves, then re-home and compare positions: more
than one full step of drift means it skipped. Keep about 15
% below the limit found.
Only proves the flow on the test printer (it can't lose
steps).
printer.cfg: max_velocity / max_accel
Orca printer profile: limits
Shrinkage
PLANNED
Measure a printed cube with calipers (ABS/ASA/PC/PA print
undersized).
Filament › Shrinkage (XY, Z)
Suggested, not yet confirmed.
Build a workflow
PLANNED
A palette of every Printune module (pre-flight, standard,
advanced, custom). Drag them into order (up/down buttons
too, for phones).
Each step keeps its own settings: ranges, step sizes, skip
if already tuned.
Order warnings, not blocks (e.g. 'flow before PA gives a
worse pick').
Custom test print
PLANNED
Upload G-code you sliced yourself, e.g. a 200 % Voron cube.
Describe the tower in Kalico TUNING_TOWER terms: COMMAND
(e.g. SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE), PARAMETER (ADVANCE), START,
then FACTOR or STEP_DELTA + STEP_HEIGHT, optional BAND.
Pick where the result goes: an Orca field or nowhere.
After the print, type the best height or band. Printune
turns it back into the value and stores it.
Any chosen Orca field, e.g. Filament › Pressure advance
Manual step
PLANNED
Instructions plus a value box, for anything Printune can't
print or measure itself.
Save and share
PLANNED
Workflows are files in printune_exports/workflows. The
standard wizard is the built-in workflow: copy it and edit
the copy.
Where results go
Orca filament preset (per filament)
Orca process / printer profile
printer.cfg (machine values)
Advice or graph only, nothing stored
Dashed box = planned, not built yet
Order within a workflow
